text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. speaker: Doctor
text: Does she recall the content of her nightmares, and do these episodes typically occur in the first half or the second half of the night? I also need to know if she has any daytime anxiety or recent stressors that might be affecting her sleep.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since she recalls the nightmares and they occur with bedtime procrastination, this points toward night terrors or anxiety rather than sleep terrors. Does she have any specific fears before going to bed, or does she resist going to sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given her ability to recall the nightmares and her bedtime procrastination, this strongly suggests nightmares disorder rather than sleep terrors.
